end.summary:
Practised identifying x-axis direction and plotting ordered pairs.
Harsh identified the second coordinate as the vertical movement and selected Quadrant II.
Initially treated (3, 2) and (2, 3) as the same point.
Later corrected this: (3, 2) means right 3, up 2; (2, 3) means right 2, up 3.
Explained the origin as the starting point for measurement and identified the first quadrant for two positive coordinates.
end.parentNote: Harsh practised reading ordered pairs by moving along the horizontal direction first and then vertically. The mix-up that (3, 2) and (2, 3) were the same point was corrected later in the lesson by describing each movement separately. At home, ask them to plot a few pairs such as (1, 4), (4, 1), and (−2, 3), saying the two movements aloud.
